title: J. R. D. Tata Flies the First Mail From Karachi, Without a Subsidy
conflicts: Initial investment Rs 200,000 (Tata heritage page, DT Next) vs Rs 1 lakh (Madras Musings); Rs 200,000 used and attributed to the group's account. Mail load: Lala's figures (55 lb Bombay, 8 lb Ahmedabad, 47 lb Madras, 6 lb Bellary) vs a circulating 25 kg; no weight used. Madras arrival 16 Oct (A Fleeting Peace) vs 17 Oct (Madras Musings); not dated in story. Proposal credited to Newall and Vintcent (Tata archives) or Vintcent alone (Wings for a Nation, JRD); story credits Vintcent, as JRD did.
notes: Funding kept as mixed: a department of Tata Sons funded with group money and run on the postal surcharge after two subsidy requests were refused. The checker's repeat screen flagged azim-premji-wipro (same-founder level) but let it through; it is a different founder and company. Quote stance: affirms. Sources lean on Tata's own heritage pages (including an excerpt of R. M. Lala's biography) with Madras Musings, DT Next and A Fleeting Peace as independent cross-checks.
